metadata.name: Vitamin D deficiency
metadata.severity: Often mild/asymptomatic; severe deficiency causes osteomalacia (adults) or rickets (children)

overview.short_description: Low vitamin D status, often asymptomatic, that can cause bone pain and muscle weakness and, when severe, osteomalacia in adults or rickets in children.
overview.detailed_description: Vitamin D deficiency is common, particularly with limited sun exposure, darker skin, covering clothing, or malabsorption. Most people are asymptomatic and identified on testing. Severe, prolonged deficiency impairs bone mineralisation (osteomalacia/rickets). Management is supplementation and addressing causes; routine screening of the whole population is not recommended - test those at risk or with suggestive features.
overview.pathophysiology: Vitamin D (from skin synthesis with sunlight and diet) is hydroxylated to 25(OH)D (the storage/measured form) then to active 1,25(OH)2D, which maintains calcium/phosphate for bone mineralisation. Deficiency causes secondary hyperparathyroidism and defective mineralisation.
overview.etiology: Reduced sunlight exposure (latitude, indoor lifestyle, covering clothing, sunscreen), darker skin, obesity (sequestration), malabsorption (coeliac, IBD, bariatric surgery), chronic kidney/liver disease, some drugs (anticonvulsants), and low dietary intake.
overview.prognosis: Excellent with treatment; osteomalacia/rickets heal with vitamin D and calcium.

prevalence.value: Very common, especially in winter, in people with darker skin, or with limited sun exposure.

epidemiology.age_groups: All ages; infants, elderly, and housebound at higher risk.
epidemiology.sex_predominance: Both; higher where clothing/cultural factors limit sun exposure.
epidemiology.geographic_distribution: Worldwide, including sunny regions where skin is covered.

risk_factors.lifestyle: Limited sun exposure, indoor lifestyle, covering clothing, consistent sunscreen use.
risk_factors.alcohol: Excess associated with poor intake/liver disease.
risk_factors.obesity: Sequestration of vitamin D in adipose tissue lowers levels.
risk_factors.genetic_factors: Rare inherited vitamin D metabolism disorders.
risk_factors.medications: Anticonvulsants, glucocorticoids, some antiretrovirals affect vitamin D metabolism.
risk_factors.previous_diseases: Malabsorption (coeliac/IBD), bariatric surgery, chronic kidney/liver disease, darker skin phototype.

chief_complaints.complaint: Aching bones / muscle weakness or pain

symptoms.symptom: Proximal muscle weakness (difficulty rising from a chair/stairs)
Children: bowed legs, growth delay, skeletal deformity (rickets)

negative_findings.why_important: Excludes vitamin D deficiency as a cause

negative_findings.finding: Normal calcium/phosphate/ALP and no bone pain/weakness

history_questions.question: Sun exposure, skin type, clothing coverage, and diet?
Any bone pain or muscle weakness?
Malabsorption symptoms, bariatric surgery, or kidney/liver disease?

physical_examination.examination: Musculoskeletal - proximal muscle power, bone tenderness

physical_examination.expected_finding: May be abnormal in severe cases

vital_signs.bmi: Higher BMI associated with lower levels

laboratory_tests.indication: In symptomatic or high-risk individuals (not population screening)
laboratory_tests.normal_range: Deficiency/insufficiency thresholds vary by guideline (commonly deficiency <25-30 nmol/L)

laboratory_tests.test_name: Calcium, phosphate, ALP, PTH (if osteomalacia/severe deficiency suspected)
laboratory_tests.expected_result: Low/normal calcium, raised ALP/PTH in osteomalacia

imaging.when_needed: Suspected osteomalacia (Looser's zones) or bone health assessment

other_diagnostic_tests.biopsy: Rarely, bone biopsy for definitive osteomalacia (not routine)

diagnostic_criteria.formal_criteria: Diagnosis by low serum 25(OH)D. Thresholds for deficiency/insufficiency vary between guidelines; interpret with clinical context and bone chemistry. Population-wide screening is not recommended - test at-risk or symptomatic individuals.

cutoff_values.value: Commonly used: deficiency 25(OH)D <25-30 nmol/L, insufficiency ~30-50 nmol/L, sufficiency >=50 nmol/L (thresholds vary; e.g., UK vs US guidance).

differential_diagnosis.disease: Other causes of bone pain/weakness (osteoporosis, osteomalacia from other causes, myopathy)
differential_diagnosis.differential_questions: Is the vitamin D normal with another bone problem?
Is the calcium low from a non-vitamin-D cause?

differential_diagnosis.differences: Normal vitamin D and bone chemistry
differential_diagnosis.differential_questions: Are labs normal despite the symptoms?

diagnostic_questions.question: Do you have limited sun exposure, darker or covered skin, or malabsorption - and any bone pain/weakness?
diagnostic_questions.purpose: Target testing to those likely to benefit
diagnostic_questions.interpretation: High-risk features or bone symptoms -> test 25(OH)D + bone chemistry

next_best_question.question: Shall we check vitamin D (and calcium/ALP/PTH if bone symptoms) and review the cause?
next_best_question.branching_logic: Deficient -> supplement and address cause; osteomalacia features -> treat and investigate; normal -> seek other explanation

red_flags.finding: Osteomalacia with fractures or severe weakness
red_flags.immediate_action: Investigate and treat; consider specialist input

referral_criteria.urgent_referral: Symptomatic hypocalcaemia; severe osteomalacia with fractures.
referral_criteria.routine_referral: Refractory deficiency, suspected malabsorption, or complex metabolic bone disease.

initial_management.supportive_care: Explain the role of vitamin D; encourage safe sun exposure and dietary sources.
initial_management.medications: Canonical schema 1.3 guidance: use treatment_guidance.medication_options and its history-based safety checks. Candidate classes/options (not a prescription): Cholecalciferol/ergocalciferol; Calcium. No autonomous selection or dosing is allowed. Source IDs: NICE_PH56, SACN_VITD.
initial_management.lifestyle_advice: Sensible sun exposure, dietary vitamin D (oily fish, fortified foods), maintenance supplementation in at-risk groups.
initial_management.follow_up: Recheck level after loading if clinically indicated; ongoing maintenance in persistent risk.
initial_management.legacy_medications_pre_v13: Vitamin D supplementation - a loading regimen for symptomatic/severe deficiency followed by maintenance, or maintenance dosing for insufficiency (per local guidance); ensure adequate calcium intake, especially if treating osteomalacia. Investigate and treat any malabsorption.

patient_education.home_advice: Vitamin D helps keep bones and muscles healthy. Low levels are common, especially with little sunlight or covered skin, and often cause no symptoms. Taking a vitamin D supplement corrects it; some people need a short higher-dose course first. Get a little safe sunlight and include vitamin D foods. See a doctor if you have bone pain, muscle weakness, or (rarely) numbness/tingling and cramps.
patient_education.home_advice_ar: فيتامين D يحافظ على صحة العظام والعضلات. انخفاضه شائع، خاصةً مع قلة الشمس أو تغطية الجلد، وغالباً بلا أعراض. تصحّحه مكمّلات فيتامين D، وبعض الناس يحتاجون جرعة أعلى قصيرة أولاً. تعرّض لقليل من الشمس الآمنة، وتناول أطعمة غنية بالفيتامين. راجع الطبيب عند ألم العظام أو ضعف العضلات، أو (نادراً) تنميل وتشنّجات.
patient_education.prevention: Adequate sun exposure/diet; supplementation in at-risk groups (infants, pregnant/breastfeeding, elderly, darker skin, covered skin).
patient_education.warning_signs: Bone pain, muscle weakness/falls, or numbness/tingling and cramps (low calcium).

prevention.lifestyle: Sensible sun exposure, dietary vitamin D, and supplementation for at-risk groups.
prevention.screening: No population screening; test at-risk/symptomatic individuals.

evidence.evidence_level: Moderate-high for treating deficiency/osteomalacia; screening not recommended for the general population.
evidence.guideline_strength: The main diagnosis/test and treatment direction was checked against the current guidance identified by NICE_PH56, SACN_VITD; see evidence_review for scope and limitations. This does not verify every legacy narrative sentence.

treatment_guidance.treatment_goal: Correct confirmed deficiency safely while preventing hypercalcaemia and addressing the cause.
treatment_guidance.legacy_narrative_summary: Canonical schema 1.3 guidance: use treatment_guidance.medication_options and its history-based safety checks. Candidate classes/options (not a prescription): Cholecalciferol/ergocalciferol; Calcium. No autonomous selection or dosing is allowed. Source IDs: NICE_PH56, SACN_VITD.
required_history_before_any_medication: age and weight where dosing is weight- or age-dependent
pregnancy or breastfeeding status when relevant
documented drug allergies and the exact reaction
all prescribed, OTC, herbal and recreational substances
major cardiovascular, respiratory, gastrointestinal and bleeding history
non_drug_measures: Safe sunlight/diet advice appropriate to skin type, culture and climate; address malabsorption or medicine causes.

medication_options.when_to_consider: Confirmed deficiency or prevention in defined risk groups using local regimen
medication_options.dose_policy: Dose is not inferred from this KB; use age, weight, renal/hepatic function, pregnancy status and the current local formulary/medicine label.

use_caution_if: renal stones, severe CKD, granulomatous disease, hyperparathyroidism, digoxin or thiazide use
monitoring: calcium and 25-hydroxyvitamin D when treating deficiency; renal function in high-risk patients

medication_options.when_to_consider: Only when dietary intake is inadequate and hypercalcaemia/stone risk is addressed
medication_options.dose_policy: Dose is not inferred from this KB; use age, weight, renal/hepatic function, pregnancy status and the current local formulary/medicine label.

use_caution_if: renal stones, CKD, hyperparathyroidism, cardiovascular risk, constipation, or interactions with levothyroxine/iron/bisphosphonates/selected antibiotics
monitoring: calcium and renal/stone risk when indicated; avoid unnecessary high total intake

medication_options.clinical_note: Do not automatically combine high-dose calcium with every vitamin D regimen.

procedures_referral_and_escalation: Specialist review for severe CKD, hypercalcaemia, granulomatous disease, recurrent stones, malabsorption or failure to respond.
treatment_guidance.localization_note: Before use in Libya, align choices with the Libyan formulary, local availability, antimicrobial resistance, referral pathways and prescribing law.
